title: MineralSoldEvent
description: One accepted sale: the actor's inventory of mineral_id went from quantity_before_kg to quantity_after_kg, its wallet from wallet_before_cr to wallet_after_cr, and the market's saturation of the mineral from saturation_before_kg (after lazy recovery) to saturation_after_kg. ONE event for the whole sale - inventory decrease and wallet increase are not split into two events (ADR-0016 section 3). Written in the SAME tick-batch transaction as the inventory, wallet and market rows and the processed_commands row (ADR-0013 section 2, ADR-0016 section 1), so for every (world, actor): wallet = sum(proceeds_cr), and for every (world, actor, mineral): inventory = sum(MINERAL_MINED.quantity_kg) - sum(MINERAL_SOLD.quantity_kg), chained through quantity_before/after across both event types in (tick, sequence) order (spec p1-03 I-80, I-81). IMPORTANCE LEVEL 0 - NOT A HISTORICAL EVENT (principle 4): the history runner passes it through as unjudged (history review p1-03 H-30..H-33). It carries every price fact a future rule needs (base, before/after price and saturation, pricing_version) because a judgement reads only the payload and the past is never recomputed (ADR-0014 section 1, principle 5). The schema cannot express the arithmetic (quantity_after = before - quantity, wallet_after = before + proceeds, proceeds = the band walk of section 4.2a); the server enforces it and QA recomputes it. actor_id and causation_id are narrowed to non-null.

actor_id.description: Narrowed from the envelope: the seller, owner of the inventory and the wallet.

causation_id.description: Narrowed from the envelope: the SELL_MINERAL command_id. Equals exactly one processed_commands.command_id and vice versa.

ship_id.description: Ship that was docked. Joins to SHIP_SPAWNED.ship_id.

pricing_version.description: The market file's pricing_version this sale was priced by - with it and the saturation pair the proceeds are recomputable after the data changes.

quantity_kg.description: Kilograms removed from the inventory and absorbed by the market. Never 0.

proceeds_cr.description: Credits added to the wallet: the band walk from saturation_before_kg over quantity_kg. >= quantity_kg because every floor price is >= 1 cr/kg (boot check).

base_price_cr_per_kg.description: The listing's band-0 price at the time of the sale - lets a future rule ask 'was this a crash from base to floor' from the payload alone.

floor_price_cr_per_kg.description: The listing's floor price at the time of the sale (base * price_floor_pct div 100) - with base and price_after a future rule decides 'did this sale hit the floor' from the payload alone, without re-reading the data table of that pricing_version (ADR-0014 section 5; history3 C-1).

price_before_cr_per_kg.description: price(band(saturation_before_kg)) - what the ticker showed just before.

price_after_cr_per_kg.description: price(band(saturation_after_kg)) - what the ticker shows just after.

saturation_before_kg.description: The market's saturation of this mineral just before the sale, AFTER applying lazy recovery up to this tick. Compare-and-set expectation of the market row.

saturation_after_kg.description: Saturation after the band walk; never above floor_band * band_kg.

quantity_before_kg.description: The actor's inventory of mineral_id before. >= quantity_kg (else INSUFFICIENT_QUANTITY). Compare-and-set expectation of the inventory row.

quantity_after_kg.description: quantity_before_kg - quantity_kg. 0 = the actor sold all of it (the row stays at 0; INVENTORY_STATE drops the item).

wallet_before_cr.description: The actor's balance before (0 if it has never sold). Compare-and-set expectation of the wallet row.
